text.p: British automotive engineering and design group Ricardo Plc said on Thursday that its board had dismissed chief executive Christopher Ross "with immediate effect" and replaced him with finance director Rodney Westhead.
Ross, who had been in the post for four years, was paid a salary of 215,000 stg and a spokesman said that negotiations to settle his compensation were continuing.
His contract stipulated a two-year notice period.
Although the company declined to comment on the reasons for the board's decision, it said in a statement that its current trading position remained in line with its latest assessment.
Ricardo's share price was unchanged following the news, with one analyst saying the news was not considered to be negative.

One industry source, who asked not to be named, said that the company had been suffering from a weakening of confidence among senior executives and replacing Ross was seen as a helpful move to restore this.
In tandem with Westhead's promotion, John Baker, managing director of the Ricardo Consulting Engineers unit, will join the board as the second of its two executive directors.
Westhead has been group finance director since 1992.
